newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The methods used by the Greater Johannesburg Metropolitan Council and its local councils to redistribute income from wealthier to poorer areas went on trial on Tuesday in the city's High Court where a group of Sandton businesses are seeking to have these methods declared unlawful.

- The fear of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve has gripped investor sentiment on the New York stock exchange, causing a collapse of nearly 300 points in the benchmark Dow Jones industrial average over two days and sparking a sharp sell-off on world bourses on Tuesday.

- The Reserve Bank's gross gold and foreign exchange reserves increased five percent to 13.1 billion rand from 12,5 billion rand last month, partly as a result of the increasing use of foreign credit lines.
- Opposition politicians chose Etienne Tsishekedi, a longtime foe of President Mobutu Sese Seko, as Zaire's prime minister on Tuesday.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's all share index lost almost two percent on Tuesday following Wall Street's huge losses on Thursday and Monday.

- Police raided the offices of six major security companies last week as part of an investigation into a 300 million rand fraud at state transport network Transnet, the Office For Serious Economic Offences confirmed on Tuesday.

- The onset of professionalism in sport is helping Southern Life make inroads into the specialised disability product market, with the institution snapping up the South African cricket team as its latest client.

- The auditor-general, the government's official watchdog over public accounts, was kept in the dark and at arm's length from an independent investigation into the Central Energy Fund, which led to the suspension of Kobus van Zyl, the general manager of the fund.
SAKE BEELD
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday did not escape the chaos on the world stock markets.
- The finance department plans to toughen its control over unspent money in government departments.
THE STAR
- Zairean soldiers continued to flee a rebel advance on Tuesday while thousands of refugees trudged desperately through the jungle away from rebel-held areas.
- The country's second biggest labour federation was officially launched on Tuesday following the merger of two federations that could transform the face of South African labour relations.

- Sandton businessmen have told the Johannesburg High Court that the city's Eastern Metropolitan Substructure has no legal right to force its ratepayers to pay the same rates as the three other councils in the Greater Johannesburg area.
